newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to shut down phone call-back firms.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to shut down phone call-back firms.

text.p: South Africa's telecommunications regulator Tuesday gave operators two weeks to shut down their telephone call-back system, which takes in revenues of 216 million rand ($46 million) annually.

In the first major ruling by the six-member South African Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (Satra), chairman Nape Maepe told a news conference call-back operations were cutting into the profits of the country's Telkom telephone monopoly.
Call-back operators offer a mechanism to take advantage of cheaper foreign rates by calling a client back after initial contact and linking them to networks outside South Africa.

Maepe said call-back systems were illegal under South Africa's 1996 Telecommunications Act, which cleared the way for the state-owned Telkom to sell a 30 percent stake to a consortium of U.S. regional Bell SBC Communications Corp. and Telekom Malaysia .
He said they also undermined Telkom's ability to extend telephone services to the black majority disadvantaged by 45 years of apartheid.
Maepe gave operators two weeks to close or face fines of up to 500,000 rand ($107,000).
Gianfranco Cicogna, chairman of the South African Callback Association, said the industry was billing about 18 million rand ($3.8 million) a month and currently was dominated by 10 operators.
He said call-back operations enhanced the international competitiveness of South African business without harming the revenue base of the domestic service provider.
However, a Telkom spokesman contested Cicogna's view, saying: "We see our international traffic sliding all the time and we can't afford it."
